title: Kuban People's Republic
capsule: The Kuban People's Republic was a short-lived Cossack state proclaimed by the Kuban Rada on January 28, 1918, declaring independence on February 16 from Soviet Russia in the territory of the former Kuban Oblast, with a population of approximately 3.5 million. Governed by an ataman and an elected rada headquartered at Yekaterinodar, it sought alignment with Ukraine and the Trans-Caucasian states against Bolshevik forces. The republic maintained a precarious independence alongside the anti-Bolshevik Volunteer Army; General Anton Denikin's forces effectively occupied it by November 1919, dissolving its independent institutions. Bolshevik forces took Yekaterinodar in March 1920, ending Cossack self-governance, with surviving rada members evacuating through Crimea.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's territorial claim corresponded to the administrative boundaries of the Kuban Oblast, which are well documented, but actual control varied rapidly during the civil war and is only approximately mappable at any given moment.
